label: D-22425b

defects.summary: When the probe launcher throws on a refusal agy itself called spent (Spent == true), DecidedOrNullAsync drops the key and parks nothing; D5 sends a failed /quota call down the 'cannot check' road, which still parks on stated/guess with the failure named, and the extra test pins the non-park.

Qualifying sends every undecided agy RateLimited to the /quota probe, including a plain text-read '429 Too Many Requests', where D2 limits 'undecided' to RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED without the quota sentence; this costs an extra agy child on an ordinary throttle.

S3 uses a constructed 'quota exhausted' reason instead of the AGY_1_3_3 sample the plan names, which is justified because the stated reset alone would end the ladder, but §12 does not record the change and the Agy133Reason constant is left unused.

§12 admits that some scenarios were not seen red first, against the Definition of Done, and leaves the extra touched files unrecorded: modelsTab.ts, resetWords.ts with spanOf exported, and architecture.md.
The refusal notice stamps itself with DateTimeOffset.UtcNow instead of the injected clock, and no test drives the PanelService wiring to Noticing.Offered: S37 checks only the onRefused callback.

summary: All 43 scenarios are present and green with both suites, the build and format clean. The structured spent verdict, the agy table reader, the locked and fail-open cooldown file, the per-key aggregation after the round, the roster exclusion, the wire member and the card all follow D1–D12 closely, and the real plan contradictions (S25's past date, S34 against S41) are resolved and recorded honestly in §12. Remaining findings are minor: a thrown probe on a spent refusal parks nothing, undecided-agy probing is broader than D2, one scenario deviation and a few touched files are not recorded, and red-first was not fully kept.
